Then we would still have to convert `torch.html#torch.flip` to `torch.flip.html#torch.flip`, note the extra `flip.` --- [t-vi]: A not quite as neat but reasonable alternative could be to see to anchors being added to the (just the link) entries of the page currently served at that URL. --- [ShawnZhong]: If I recall correctly, pytorch.org is served by GitHub pages, which does not allow server configurations (say URL rewrite), but client-side redirects should be an option. For adding anchors, I didn't see native support in Sphinx to generate anchors for `autosummary`. I guess we either need to hack into Sphinx or manually add them. --- [vadimkantorov]: @ShawnZhong > Then we would still have to convert `torch.html#torch.flip` to `torch.flip.html#torch.flip`, note the extra `flip.` Even in that case, maybe better to remove "generated"? Since it will be in every URL, it's a bit cleaner without it, and it carries no special meaning, docs are (almost) always generated --- [ShawnZhong]: Not sure exactly why, but it seems that some popular python libs have `generated` in the docs: - https://numpy.org/doc/1.18/reference/generated/numpy.add.html - https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.randint.html - http://ipython.org/ipython-doc/stable/api/generated/IPython.config.application.html Maybe @mattip knows more about this. --- [ShawnZhong]: One of the minor benefits I can think of is it's easier to add a single `generated` folder to `.gitignore` and to delete all generated files. --- [vadimkantorov]: Well, I was just worried that in future if scheme changes, there would be a lot of hyperlinks on the internet containing that "generated" thing. But it's not much important --- [vadimkantorov]: Also there would be a challenge to remove old pages from Google search which is quite nasty (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/3428). It would be unfortunate, if Google search finds both new and old links. By the way, NumPy/SciPy do a bad job here... cc @zou3519 tldr: to remove reliably it's better to generate old pages as well, but set some special headers that would instruct Google to de-index them. And only later to disable their generation --- [mattip]: > One of the minor benefits I can think of is it's easier to add a single generated folder to .gitignore and to delete all generated files This seems to be the motivation, and the use of `generated` is standard across projects that use sphinx. > A not quite as neat but reasonable alternative could be to add to anchors being added to the (just the link) entries of the page currently served at that URL. If we post-process all the html, we could add an anchor for these entries: - add an id for the tag - add an anchor element to create the anchor link to the id. For example `

¶ Google search results should not be spilled with both old and new URL versions Hmm. Not sure how to give a lower rank to the top-level documents than to the generated ones. It seems the tools available in robots.txt or meta tags are binary: either include or exclude whole pages. Perhaps if we use the javascript solution in gh-39032 but then exclude robots from seeing the javascript that would help? Of course users who turn off javascript would also not see the anchor-specific links and would be refered to the top of the pages ... --- [vadimkantorov]: @zou3519 should have more insights about Google indexing hacking :) --- [vadimkantorov]: @mattip about dichotomy between "top-level documents than to the generated ones.". I'm not sure I understand you. If by "top-level documents" you mean old pages, I think they should be phased out from Google search index, by first modifying their meta and simultaneously publishing new indexable pages. Like that, old links will continue to work and Google will not index old pages over time --- [t-vi]: You'd want to have a list of available functions somewhere, ideally with link and one-line synopsis. --- [vadimkantorov]: Well, maybe the "top-level" / index pages could be created manually/automagically, then old links could stay, and anchors would work. Okay, they will be large, but much faster to load than before, because they would only contain links to new separate pages --- [mattip]: The old links have become summaries. So the "old link" that points to this [whole documentation blurb](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/torch.html#torch.allclose) on `stable`, now points to [the allclose line in the table](https://pytorch.org/docs/master/torch.html#comparison-ops) in `master` after this PR. Clicking on the `allclose` link brings you to the [full documentation](https://pytorch.org/docs/master/generated/torch.allclose.html#torch.allclose). I wouldn;t want to totally disable indexing the summary page. since there is still useful information on it, for instance the documentation about [`torch.no_grad`](https://pytorch.org/docs/master/torch.html#locally-disabling-gradient-computation), so --- [vadimkantorov]: The old link "https://pytorch.org/docs/master/torch.html#torch.flip" still does not work (just checked). I'm all for summary pages, but the new summary pages do not have right anchors, so the browser does not scroll down automatically, and this is problematic --- [t-vi]: That's because #39086 isn't merged yet. :) --- [vadimkantorov]: oh, makes sense :) --- [vadimkantorov]: Some urls got broken again :( https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch.github.io/issues/599 --- [malfet]: @svekars do we have a mechanism to detect if new broken links are added to the docs? --- [mikaylagawarecki]: fyi @svekars Summarizing discussion from triage meeting: There are two types of broken links 1. broken links within our docs 2. external links that are broken We should have a mechanism for detecting and eliminating (1). For external docs probably need to use something else - there is [sphinx-reredirects](https://documatt.com/sphinx-reredirects/index.html) extension for example. There should be a way to detect that a page is being moved in a PR and that a redirect must be created. --- [vadimkantorov]: I think a problem is that for this anchor -> page factor-outs, the redirects should be done in a manual JavaScript hack comparing window.location.hash to some known list of redirects. Or at least, the HTML anchors should be preserved so that https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/nn.html#torch.nn.Embedding scrolls to something reasonable (at least some table row)

stage1.title: Make DDP failure recoverable
stage1.body:
@kuttas @pietern and I had a discussion on how to make DDP failure recoverable. The process involves the following steps:

```python
m = SomeModel()
dist.init_process_group()
ddp = DistributedDataParallel(m)
# got error
dist.destroy_process_group()
dist.init_process_group()
del ddp
ddp = DistributedDataParallel(m)
```

This does not work in today's DDP. Currently, to get better performance, DDP assigns the [original module](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fa4ca4e70e98fbe944d1435929ea4fd17c7bed7d/torch/nn/parallel/distributed.py#L316) to the first module replica instead of creating a new one. Then, it creates a new `Reducer` to [add post hooks](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fa4ca4e70e98fbe944d1435929ea4fd17c7bed7d/torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/reducer.cpp#L108-L112) to sync params. However, because every reconstructed DDP instance wraps the same original module, all their reducers will add hooks to the same set of variables. Hence, after 10 recoveries, each param (variable) in the original module will have 11 hooks introduced by 11 different reducers, where only the last one is still alive. We thought about several potential solutions:

#### Solution 1: Force Module Replication

Force DDP to create new module replicas instead of using the original module. In this way, those variables in the replicas will die together with the DDP instance. But it will make the DDP slower. Maybe make it an option?

#### Solution 2: Delete Hooks in Destructor

I feel the best way would be deleting those hooks from model variables when destructing a `Reducer`, but I didn't find a clean way to do that. The [`add_post_hook`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fa4ca4e70e98fbe944d1435929ea4fd17c7bed7d/torch/csrc/autograd/function.h#L250) function takes unique parameters, and we can get those hooks through [`post_hooks`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fa4ca4e70e98fbe944d1435929ea4fd17c7bed7d/torch/csrc/autograd/function.h#L254). Directly looping through the the hooks vector and find the target to delete seems to be too hackish.

#### Solution 3: Create New Variables (?)

Not sure if this can work. Instead of creating replica (as in Solution 1), let DDP create a new variable for every parameter in the original module. All DDP forward and backward pass will use those new variables. I think this won't work if the application only wraps part of the model using DDP, because there will be two disjoint autograd graphs (?)


@soumith @gchanan @ezyang  thoughts?

stage3_gold.comments:
[mdlockyer]: I recently posted about this in the discussion forum [here](https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/safely-removing-a-module-from-ddp/45753). This issue actually both answers my question and confirms what I suspected was the case when either removing the module, or in this case, trying to redo the DDP wrapping. The idea of removing the hooks during destruction of the reducer would make DDP much more flexible as well. It would not only solve the situation described in this issue, but would also allow for a module to be removed from DDP with something like:

    model = ddp_model.module
    del ddp

I'm currently working on an architecture that would benefit greatly from the ability to easily remove the module from DDP. Right now there is a lot of extra complexity in my codebase just to deal with this.

---

[kuttas]: @MichaelDylan77  what are you doing to work around it currently? Re-create the inner model and transfer the parameters over?

The usage pattern you have above is similar to the use case I have. I need to be able to re-create the DDP module-wrapper with a new set of worker machines and keep training.

---

[mdlockyer]: That's exactly right. I have to re-instantiate the model and copy params. It's a pain right now. It's nice to know someone else has a use case in which they would need to extract the model from DDP 👍. It seemed like an edge case.

---

[mrshenli]: ## Trying Solution 2

#21534 seems addressed the problem but in quite a dirty way. A better solution might need to satisfy the following requirements:

1. As mentioned by @pietern, the hook deletion function should be implemented in `torch/csrc/autograd/function.h`, as it owns the data. 
2. We should not slow down existing use cases of `add_post_hook` and `post_hooks()`.

I initially thought about using an `OrderedDict` to store named hooks, as what we did for params, buffers, and children in `nn/Module.h`, but that would violate the second requirement.

~Another possibility is that, instead of using the default deleter, we create a special deleter for the hook unique ptr in DDP, e.g., `ReducerHookDeleter`, that wraps the default deleter.  The `add_post_hook` and `post_hooks()` APIs would stay the same, then we add one `delete_post_hook<DeleterType>()` API to `torch/csrc/autograd/function.h`, which loops over all post hooks, and only delete the ones with matching deleter type, i.e., `ReducerHookDeleter`. This would be slow, but is OK, as we only need this on failures, where timeout delay will dominate. Any comments?~ Should be able to directly check hook pointer type.

---

[pietern]: @MichaelDylan77 Could you give the code in #21591 a try and see if it works for you?

---

[mdlockyer]: @pietern I’ll test it out this afternoon!

---

[mdlockyer]: Everything seems to work fine on my end. No obvious issues. Memory usage looks relatively constant after removing and re-wrapping the model in DDP

---

[pietern]: @MichaelDylan77 Thanks for confirming it works for you!

---

[knagrecha]: Same issue is now coming up for FSDP - but I suspect it'll be a harder fix there due to how FSDP recursively injects itself. Can't just pull it out in this way.

stage1.title: Very high CPU utilization with pin_memory=True and num_workers > 0
stage1.body:
## 🐛 Bug
There seems to be an issue with CPU utilization when using a DataLoader with pin_memory=True and num_workers > 0. 

I revisited some old code that had `pin_memory=True` and two workers that weren't doing all that much. It pinned all of my CPU cores at or near 100%, with 40-50% of the usage in the kernel.  I've had performance issues with pinned memory in the past, but never to this level. Indeed, I cannot reproduce the issue going back to some older environments with 0.4 or 1.0.1. But on 3 machines w/ PyTorch 1.1 and 1.2 I can easily reproduce by running the MNIST main.py from the current examples master.

If I set either num_workers=0 or pin_memory=False the issue goes away and I'm left with the expected one core and change of usage for MNIST (or two cores and change for my original case). 

## To Reproduce

1. Run `main.py` from the MNIST example on master pytorch/examples repository.

## Expected behavior

For MNIST, with 1 worker I expect roughly 1 core's worth of CPU utilization plus some overhead. It consumes 50-100% of all cores on systems with 8-14 physical (16-28 logical) cores. A large % of the CPU usage is in the kernel, appears to be spinning/yielding, possibly due to contention. 

## Environment

I've reproduced on 3 machines.

 - PyTorch Version (e.g., 1.0): 1.1 and 1.2 (no issue on an older 1.0.1 and 0.4.1 environment on one of the machines)
 - OS (e.g., Linux): two Ubuntu 18.04 machines, one Ubuntu 16.04 machine
 - How you installed PyTorch (`conda`, `pip`, source): All conda installs
 - Python version: 3.7.3 and 3.6.8
 - CUDA/cuDNN version: Cuda 10 and CUDNN 7.5.1 and 7.6.2
 - GPU models and configuration: dual Titan RTX one one machine, dual Titan Xp and 1080Ti on other two
 - Any other relevant information:

## Additional context
I've seen at least one very likely, and other potential threads in discussion forum that are likely this issue. 

This one has an htop screenshot from me, and another user:
https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/cpu-usage-extremely-high/52172/5



cc @SsnL

model_evidence.title: Very high CPU utilization with pin_memory=True and num_workers > 0
model_evidence.body:
## 🐛 Bug
There seems to be an issue with CPU utilization when using a DataLoader with pin_memory=True and num_workers > 0. 

I revisited some old code that had `pin_memory=True` and two workers that weren't doing all that much. It pinned all of my CPU cores at or near 100%, with 40-50% of the usage in the kernel.  I've had performance issues with pinned memory in the past, but never to this level. Indeed, I cannot reproduce the issue going back to some older environments with 0.4 or 1.0.1. But on 3 machines w/ PyTorch 1.1 and 1.2 I can easily reproduce by running the MNIST main.py from the current examples master.

If I set either num_workers=0 or pin_memory=False the issue goes away and I'm left with the expected one core and change of usage for MNIST (or two cores and change for my original case). 

## To Reproduce

1. Run `main.py` from the MNIST example on master pytorch/examples repository.

## Expected behavior

For MNIST, with 1 worker I expect roughly 1 core's worth of CPU utilization plus some overhead. It consumes 50-100% of all cores on systems with 8-14 physical (16-28 logical) cores. A large % of the CPU usage is in the kernel, appears to be spinning/yielding, possibly due to contention. 

## Environment

I've reproduced on 3 machines.

 - PyTorch Version (e.g., 1.0): 1.1 and 1.2 (no issue on an older 1.0.1 and 0.4.1 environment on one of the machines)
 - OS (e.g., Linux): two Ubuntu 18.04 machines, one Ubuntu 16.04 machine
 - How you installed PyTorch (`conda`, `pip`, source): All conda installs
 - Python version: 3.7.3 and 3.6.8
 - CUDA/cuDNN version: Cuda 10 and CUDNN 7.5.1 and 7.6.2
 - GPU models and configuration: dual Titan RTX one one machine, dual Titan Xp and 1080Ti on other two
 - Any other relevant information:

## Additional context
I've seen at least one very likely, and other potential threads in discussion forum that are likely this issue. 

This one has an htop screenshot from me, and another user:
https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/cpu-usage-extremely-high/52172/5



cc @SsnL

stage1.title: DataLoader fails to re-raise exceptions with required arguments
stage1.body:
## 🐛 Bug
`torch.utils.data.DataLoader` attempts to relay exceptions from its child processes.  It fails to do this when the exception type takes multiple required arguments.

## To Reproduce

Run this:
```
import torch.utils.data
class E(Exception):
    def __init__(self, a, b):
        pass
    def __str__(self):
        return "Special exception message"

class G(torch.utils.data.IterableDataset):
    def __iter__(self):
        raise E(a=1, b=2)
        yield 1
    
d = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(G(), num_workers=1)
next(iter(d))
```

The result:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/usr/local/miniconda3/envs/openai/lib/python3.7/site-packages/torch/utils/data/dataloader.py", line 819, in __next__
    return self._process_data(data)
  File "/usr/local/miniconda3/envs/openai/lib/python3.7/site-packages/torch/utils/data/dataloader.py", line 846, in _process_data
    data.reraise()
  File "/usr/local/miniconda3/envs/openai/lib/python3.7/site-packages/torch/_utils.py", line 369, in reraise
    raise self.exc_type(msg)
TypeError: __init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'b'
```

Should see the `E: Special exception message` printed. (This works when `num_workers=0`.)

stage1.body:
## 📚 Documentation

#### Link

https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html#torch.distributed.all_reduce_multigpu

#### API

`torch.distributed.all_reduce_multigpu`

#### Issue

In the "Parameters" section, there is an input `list`, but it is not in the signature, and it is not accepted by the function. It should be `tensor_list`

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24580222/91068305-1b443780-e602-11ea-8e9f-c065e3ac5092.png)


Running code :

~~~python
import torch
torch.distributed.all_reduce_multigpu(list=[])
~~~

gives exception 

~~~python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
TypeError: all_reduce_multigpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'list'
~~~



#### **System information**

- OS: MacOS Mojave 10.14
- PyTorch version:  1.6.0
- Python version: 3.8.2

cc @jlin27
